candidates.tagline: Amazon removed Kindle's buttons. Now sells you the buttons back for $35.
candidates.story: Amazon discontinued the Kindle Oasis — its last e-reader with physical page-turn buttons — in 2024, saying 'all our devices are touch-forward which is what our customers are comfortable with'; then on October 1, 2026, launched the $34.99 Kindle Click Bluetooth remote and a $79.99 Page-Turn Cover with built-in physical buttons so readers can turn pages without touching their touchscreen Kindle.
candidates.why_funny: The company that spent years removing buttons and insisting touchscreens were the future is now charging premium prices to sell the past back to you as optional accessories.
candidates.alt: The Amazon Kindle Click, a small white Bluetooth remote with two round page-turn buttons, resting next to a new Amazon Kindle e-reader

candidates.tagline: $1.1 billion in 'nearly impossible to evade' NYC subway gates — they held an Olympics jumping over them.
candidates.story: In January 2026, New York riders held a viral 'Fare Evasion Olympics' at the MTA's new prototype fare gates — a pole dancer, a parkour athlete, and a blindfolded man with a cane all slipped through — yet on October 7, 2026, Governor Hochul announced a $1.1 billion contract to expand the same gates to 150 more subway stations, describing them as 'nearly impossible to evade.'
candidates.why_funny: The gates that spawned a competitive sport for bypassing them are now the centerpiece of a billion-dollar infrastructure rollout, still officially branded as 'nearly impossible' to get through.
candidates.alt: New modern saloon-style sliding fare gates at a New York City subway station, with wide glass panels replacing traditional rotating turnstiles
